solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: When upset, youth leaves for lunch?

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the little word is turned upside down, read from the bottom up

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: A teenager storms off at lunchtime after getting upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like the verb whose subject is the youth; it is the plural noun, salad greens, and the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of lettuce and other greens is a typical light midday meal, hence leaves eaten at lunch.

clue.text: All others fall: hold back!

parts.note: the rest means all the others
rain is what falls from the sky, a fall of rain

explanation.surface: A commander shouts to stop the troops while everyone else is tumbling down.
explanation.definitionFit: To curb or check something is to hold it back, a straightforward synonym used as an imperative.

clue.text: A flirt with no worries

parts.note: a flirt can be called a tease, someone who leads others on

explanation.surface: Describes a carefree coquette who never frets.
explanation.definitionFit: Being relaxed and comfortable means having no worries, the military stand-easy phrase in its everyday sense.

clue.text: In good order, arms given up

indicators.note: in a down clue, given up means the word is turned upwards, read from the bottom

parts.note: guns are arms, weapons

explanation.surface: Soldiers surrender their weapons neatly and in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given up' looks like surrender, but in a down clue it signals reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Snug can mean neat, trim and well arranged, as a ship kept tidy and shipshape.

clue.text: Cat runs after its prey

indicators.note: after places the runs letter behind the prey word in the answer

parts.note: a cat's prey is a mouse
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cat chases off after something it wants to catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' looks like the verb of the sentence; it is R, behind MOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat valued for catching vermin is called by this name, a specific kind of feline.

clue.text: Showing reluctance, northern monarch shoulders honorific Indian title

indicators.note: in a down clue, the monarch shoulders the title: it is carried on top, so the title comes first

parts.note: Shri (or Sri) is an Indian title of respect, like Mr
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A northern king reluctantly takes on the burden of a grand Indian title.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging back or recoiling out of timidity is a display of reluctance, so the adjective fits.

clue.text: Secret devotee of Latin, even in translation

indicators.note: translation turns the words into something else, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hidden admirer of the Latin language, even when it is rendered into English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in translation' rearranges LATIN EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A card sent anonymously on 14 February comes from an admirer, and the sender is so named.

clue.text: Little hut for Mac and Morag as well, with yard

definitions.text: Little hut for Mac and Morag

parts.note: both can mean as well, too, in 'both him and her'

explanation.surface: A small hut made for two Scots, who also get a yard.
explanation.walkthrough: Mac and Morag stand for Scots in general: a bothy is a Scottish mountain shelter or farmworkers' hut.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a simple cottage or refuge in the hills is called by this name, a regional word.

clue.text: Islam's regulated prayer book

indicators.note: regulated means put into a set order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Describes a rule-bound Muslim book of prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regulated' rearranges ISLAMS; the surface's Islam is a decoy, as the answer is a Catholic book.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of the texts for celebrating Mass through the year is a Christian service book.

clue.text: Source of danger lacking power in sacred text

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the power letter is removed

parts.note: a mantrap, a hidden trap for trespassers, is a source of danger
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A holy text that poses no threat without its power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes P from MANTRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A word or verse chanted in Hindu or Buddhist meditation is a holy utterance, so a sacred text.

clue.text: Took exception to profits and material help

parts.note: gains are profits
aid is practical, material help

explanation.surface: Someone objected to both the profits and the handouts.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny or contradict a statement is to object to it, hence taking exception.

clue.text: Most basic bank website ignoring the odds

parts.note: a bar is a bank of sand or shingle in a river or sea

indicators.note: ignoring the odd letters leaves only the second, fourth and sixth of the word

explanation.surface: A minimal banking website that pays no heed to risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring the odds' keeps the even letters of website, E S T.
explanation.definitionFit: The barest necessities are the most minimal ones, the superlative of plain or minimal.

clue.text: Criminal one caught by the force

indicators.note: caught by means held inside, so the one letter sits within the others

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
F is the abbreviation for force in physics

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker is arrested by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the force' looks like the police; it is THE plus F, with I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A robber or stealer is a lawbreaker, so a criminal noun fits.

clue.text: Pet butterfly, say

definitions.meaning: to pet is to caress an animal with the hand
butterfly is one swimming technique, like breaststroke

explanation.surface: A pet butterfly, as though someone kept one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like a noun qualifying butterfly; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Caressing with the hand is the verb sense; a swimming style such as butterfly is the noun sense.

clue.text: Obvious issue with middle of religious chant

parts.note: plain means obvious
a son is issue, offspring

indicators.note: middle of takes the central letter of the nine-letter word

explanation.surface: A clear matter about the core of a sacred chant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'religious chant' reads as one phrase, but 'middle of religious' gives G, leaving 'chant' alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaccompanied medieval church music sung in unison, like Gregorian chant, is this kind of liturgical singing.

clue.text: Tart left in cooler

indicators.note: in places the left letter within the word for the cooler

parts.note: a fan cools you

explanation.surface: A tart has been put in the fridge to cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside FAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An open pastry case with a filling is a kind of tart.

clue.text: Inactive liquor apparatus

definitions.meaning: the equipment for distilling spirits such as whisky

explanation.surface: A distilling machine that is not running.
explanation.definitionFit: Motionless is the adjective sense; a distiller's vessel for making spirits is the noun sense.

clue.text: Recoil about worker's crude shelter

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to shy is to recoil, as a startled horse does
an ant is the crossword's usual worker, with 's read as is

explanation.surface: Someone flinches at a labourer's rough hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recoil' looks like the verb of the sentence, but it is the outer word; the ant is crosswordland's standard worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A roughly built hut or shack is a makeshift dwelling, a rude shelter.

clue.text: Commonly quit humbug

definitions.meaning: colloquially, to do a runner or abscond, as in the slang phrase 'do a ...'

explanation.surface: Someone casually gives up the pretence and nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commonly' marks slang: British 'do a bunk' means run away.
explanation.definitionFit: To scarper is the slang sense of leaving; nonsense or claptrap is the noun sense of humbug.

clue.text: Treacherously water-borne but neither English nor European pest

indicators.note: treacherously suggests letters behaving unreliably, so they are rearranged
neither, paired with nor, says that one of the letters is not wanted, so it is removed from the fodder
nor, completing neither, says the second letter is also not wanted and is removed too

explanation.surface: A rodent swims dangerously, bringing disease, though not from England or Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neither ... nor' removes both Es from WATERBORNE, leaving WATRBORN, which 'Treacherously' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The common large rodent of sewers and farms is an example of vermin, a pest.

clue.text: Duke holding base adult party

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the base letter goes inside

parts.note: dukes are fists in slang, as in 'put up your dukes'
e is the base of natural logarithms
A is the abbreviation for adult, the old film rating

explanation.surface: A nobleman throws a party for grown-ups at a base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duke' looks like the nobleman; it is slang for a fist.
explanation.definitionFit: A festival or celebration in Spanish-speaking lands is a party.

clue.text: Surge of rising river essentially overwhelming

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word reads upwards

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England

indicators.note: essentially means at its essence, the centre, so the middle two letters are taken

explanation.surface: A river in flood rises and overwhelms everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns TEES to SEET; 'essentially' takes HE from overwhelming.
explanation.definitionFit: To churn, boil and heave like rough water is to surge.

clue.text: Brawl after anger almost produces depression

indicators.note: after places the brawl word behind the trimmed anger word
almost means the word stops one letter short

parts.note: fury is anger
a row is a noisy quarrel or brawl

explanation.surface: A fight following rage nearly leads to depression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims FURY to FUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A groove or trench in a field, or a frown line, is a hollow, a depression.

clue.text: More risky section of cutter?

definitions.meaning: more reckless, comparative of hasty and imprudent
a cutter is a pig reared for meat; a slice of its bacon is the section meant

explanation.surface: A riskier piece of a boat or blade.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'cutter' looks like a boat or blade; it is a pig grown for bacon, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Being more reckless is the comparative adjective; a thin slice of bacon is the noun sense.

clue.text: Four managed outside and survived

indicators.note: the managed word goes outside, around the numeral

parts.note: led means managed, was in charge of
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four people coped and came through alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Four' looks like a count of people; it is the Roman numeral, held by the word for managed.
explanation.definitionFit: Having stayed alive through something is having survived it.

clue.text: American appeal for help securing top quality insulating material

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the distress signal surrounds the quality word

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
best means of top quality

explanation.surface: An American pleads for the finest insulation.
explanation.definitionFit: A fibrous mineral once widely used for fireproofing and lagging is a heat-resistant lining.

clue.text: Celebrated 4, name dropping

indicators.note: in a down clue, dropping moves the name letter lower in the word

parts.note: the clue points to the answer at 4 down

explanation.surface: A cross-reference that drops a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' takes N from second place and lets it fall one place down the column.
explanation.definitionFit: Praised, lauded in song or verse, as in 'unsung heroes' who go uncelebrated.

clue.text: Twisted nose is comely in Scotland

indicators.note: twisted means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crooked nose is considered attractive north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisted' rearranges NOSE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots word for buxom, attractive and pleasant-looking, a regional synonym.

clue.text: Chilli used in Mexican chowder

indicators.note: used in means the letters are found within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A chilli pepper goes into a Mexican soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' finds the letters across mexicAN CHOwder.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried poblano pepper of Mexican cooking is a kind of chilli.

clue.text: Doddery elder aunt, not linked by blood

indicators.note: doddery means shaky and unsteady, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A frail old aunt turns out not to be family after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doddery' rearranges ELDER AUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: People with no family tie, no kinship, are not connected by blood.
